gaps.title: Excel export not represented in the mockup
gaps.description: REQ-004 (must) requires export to Excel and DEC-002 confirms both PDF and Excel are needed, but the only export action shown in the capture is a row-level "Export PDF" button. No Excel export action, its scope (single invoice or many), or the invoice fields it includes are shown in the capture or stated in the requirements.
gaps.why_it_matters: Excel export is a confirmed must-have for the invoice list, yet nothing in the mockup shows where it is triggered, whether it covers one invoice or a set, or what columns it contains.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The Excel export cannot be specified or designed; a must-have requirement would ship unmet or be built to guessed scope and content.
research_questions: What are established practices for exporting financial records such as invoices to Excel (.xlsx versus .csv), including handling of currency amounts and dates?
What spreadsheet formula injection (CSV/Excel injection) risks apply to exporting user-entered fields such as customer names, per OWASP guidance?

gaps.title: No recovery path for deleted invoices, and recovery permissions undefined
gaps.description: REQ-006 (must) and DEC-003 require deleted invoices to be recoverable for 30 days, but the capture shows no screen, list, or action for viewing or restoring deleted invoices. DEC-004's answer restates the 30-day window and permanent removal but does not say who can recover a deleted invoice.
gaps.why_it_matters: Recovery within 30 days is a confirmed must-have for invoice deletion, but there is no observed place to find deleted invoices and no decision on whether only finance administrators, or also others, may restore them.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The recovery feature cannot be specified; deleted invoices may be unrecoverable in practice, or recoverable by the wrong people.

gaps.title: Permanent invoice deletion versus financial record-keeping obligations
gaps.description: DEC-003 confirms invoices are permanently removed 30 days after deletion. Invoices are financial records (amounts shown in GBP), and the requirements do not state whether any legal or accounting record-retention obligation limits deleting them, or whether certain invoices (for example sent or paid) must be retained.
gaps.why_it_matters: Permanently deleting issued invoices may conflict with statutory retention of accounting and VAT records, and a sequential invoice-number series (INV-3301) may become gapped.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The product could destroy records the customer is legally required to keep, exposing them to compliance and audit risk.
research_questions: What do HMRC rules (VAT Notice 700/21 and Companies Act 2006 accounting records duties) require for retaining issued sales invoices in the UK, and for how long?
Do UK VAT rules permit deleting an issued invoice, or must it be cancelled or credited while the original record is retained?

gaps.title: Finance administrator role undefined and Delete visibility for other users unobserved
gaps.description: DEC-001 confirms only finance administrators may delete invoices and other users cannot. The requirements do not define who is a finance administrator or how that role is assigned, and the capture shows the Delete button enabled in a single state with no indication of how it appears for users without the role.
gaps.why_it_matters: Deletion of invoices is restricted to one role, but without a definition of that role and the non-admin view of the Delete action, the restriction cannot be specified or tested.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Non-administrators may be shown or able to use Delete, or the wrong people may be granted the role.

gaps.title: Delete confirmation and invoice-state restrictions unanswered
gaps.description: The capture does not show whether Delete asks for confirmation, and no requirement or decision says whether invoices in any state (for example draft, sent, paid) may be deleted.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-002: confirmation step; deletable regardless of status

gaps.why_it_matters: Delete sits as a single enabled button on each invoice row next to Export PDF; whether a mis-click removes an invoice, and whether paid or sent invoices are protected, is not settled.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Invoices may be deleted accidentally or deleted after being issued or paid, creating data and accounting errors.
research_questions: What confirmation patterns do established accounting products (for example Xero, QuickBooks) use before deleting or voiding an invoice, and do they restrict deletion by invoice status?

gaps.title: Downstream effects of deleting and restoring an invoice
gaps.description: Neither the requirements nor the capture say what happens to customer balances, reports, totals, or related records while an invoice is deleted-but-recoverable, when it is restored, or when it is permanently removed, nor whether deleted invoices remain visible in the invoice list during the 30 days.
gaps.why_it_matters: Invoices carry amounts tied to a customer (Northwind, £1,200); a soft-deleted invoice that still counts, or stops counting, changes balances the customer relies on.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Balances and reports may be inconsistent across the delete, restore, and permanent-removal steps.

gaps.title: Audit trail for delete, restore and permanent removal
gaps.description: No requirement or decision states whether deleting, restoring, or permanently removing an invoice must be recorded (who, what, when), or whether that record survives the invoice's permanent removal.
gaps.why_it_matters: Deletion of financial records is restricted to one role and ends in permanent removal; without a trace, it cannot later be shown who removed an invoice.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Disputed or mistaken deletions cannot be investigated after the 30-day window.
research_questions: What audit-trail expectations apply to deletion of accounting records under UK record-keeping guidance (for example HMRC Making Tax Digital digital-links and record requirements)?

gaps.title: PDF export content, delivery and permissions unspecified
gaps.description: The capture shows a row-level Export PDF button with no target. The requirements and decisions do not state who may export, what the PDF contains, its layout, or how it is delivered.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-002: export permissions, format, delivery

gaps.why_it_matters: PDF export is a confirmed must-have and the PDF is likely to be what customers receive as the invoice, so its content and who can produce it matter.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The PDF cannot be specified; exported invoices may omit details or be produced by users who should not.
research_questions: What information must a valid UK VAT invoice contain (HMRC VAT Notice 700/21 section on invoice contents)?

gaps.title: Empty, loading, success and error states not shown
gaps.description: Only the default state of the Invoices screen was captured. The empty list, loading, success after delete or export, and failure states for Delete and Export are not shown in the capture.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-002: Delete fails; Export PDF fails

gaps.why_it_matters: Both actions on this screen change or produce financial records; users need to know whether a delete or export succeeded.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users may repeat deletes or exports, or believe an invoice is gone or exported when it is not.

gaps.title: Accessibility of row actions in the invoices table
gaps.description: The actions column in the invoices table is unlabelled, and each row's buttons are labelled only "Delete" and "Export PDF" with no reference to the invoice they act on. Keyboard, focus and status-message behaviour are not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: With many rows, screen-reader users would hear repeated identical "Delete" buttons, which raises the risk of deleting the wrong invoice.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The screen may fail WCAG 2.2 AA and assistive-technology users may act on the wrong invoice.
research_questions: How do WCAG 2.2 success criteria 1.3.1, 2.4.6, 4.1.2 and 4.1.3 apply to repeated row-level action buttons and table header labelling in data tables?

gaps.title: Scope of permanent removal after 30 days
gaps.description: The requirements do not say whether permanent removal after 30 days also covers backups, previously exported PDF or Excel files, or audit records, or whether anyone is told before removal.
gaps.why_it_matters: "Removed permanently" is a confirmed outcome but its reach is undefined for this product's invoice data.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Invoice data may persist where the customer expects it gone, or be lost where they expect it kept.

gaps.title: Repeated or concurrent delete and export actions
gaps.description: Not stated what happens if Delete is pressed twice, if two finance administrators act on the same invoice at once, or if an invoice is exported while another user deletes it.
gaps.why_it_matters: Delete and export act on the same invoice row and deletion is time-limited before permanent removal.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users may see stale invoices or export records that have already been deleted.

assumptions.text: DEC-001 (only finance administrators delete; other users cannot) is treated as overriding REQ-002 (any user can delete invoices they created), even though the registry shows REQ-002 as approved.
assumptions.why: The decision answers the permission conflict, but REQ-002 was approved rather than superseded.
assumptions.impact: No gap is raised for creator-based deletion; GAP-004 assumes a single deleting role.
assumptions.to_confirm: Whether REQ-002 should be marked superseded by DEC-001.

assumptions.text: DEC-004 is treated as answering what happens after 30 days (permanent removal) but not who can recover a deleted invoice.
assumptions.why: The DEC-004 verbatim repeats the DEC-003 answer and is silent on recovery permissions.
assumptions.impact: Recovery permissions remain open in GAP-002.
assumptions.to_confirm: Who may restore a deleted invoice.

assumptions.text: The product is used in a UK context, inferred from GBP amounts in the capture.
assumptions.why: Needed to name relevant record-retention and invoice-content rules in research questions.
assumptions.impact: Research for GAP-003, GAP-007 and GAP-008 targets UK rules.
assumptions.to_confirm: Which jurisdictions the customer's invoices fall under.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Excel export scope (single or multiple invoices), fields and placement are not stated and not shown in the mockup.
Who can recover a deleted invoice and where recovery happens are not stated; DEC-004 does not answer it.
The finance administrator role is not defined.
